<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via callbackURL (literal, a string literal in runDirectSignIn), phone_number (literal, a string literal in otherSignInMethods))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via callbackURL (literal, a string literal in runDirectSignIn))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via phone_number (literal, a string literal in otherSignInMethods))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via callbackURL (literal, a string literal in runDirectSignIn))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9f8e2fc6d8ac8c79bb110b727cc583c1a5ee23cb` — the merge of head `4cf17caabd606319a63ffc071e6061f75361156f` into base `4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9f8e2fc6d8ac8c79bb110b727cc583c1a5ee23cb && git checkout 9f8e2fc6d8ac8c79bb110b727cc583c1a5ee23cb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b 4cf17caabd606319a63ffc071e6061f75361156f && git checkout -B drift-repro 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b && git merge --no-ff 4cf17caabd606319a63ffc071e6061f75361156f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4c32b9694b7b248646b2053b6eafea2cc212693b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2a03b651b6bf0df1bb20a4ea831111617662fb7a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `.changeset/33358-local-sign-in-off-floor.md`, `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/direct-sign-in.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/direct-sign-in.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts`

Read: the PR's four commits on top of `c32bb6cc` (`623d63fa`, `a72de75a`, `773e81c7`, `2a03b651`): 6 files, +295/−22. I compared the floor's predicate with the page's own (`ui/packages/auth/src/LoginForm.tsx:349-354`), the served value (`auth-manager.ts:5928`) and the Console's retry logic (`ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/directSignIn.ts:79`). I read how better-auth 1.7.12 and `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 add `error` to `errorCallbackURL`. I ran no repo test or build. I ran a scratch copy of `keptReturnPath` and `carriedRedirect` against the foreign spellings listed below.

### ① Derived judgments

**Items 3 and 4: the carried redirect uses the door's own return-path rule. I found no open redirect.**
- *Same validator.* `carriedRedirect` (`direct-sign-in.ts:221-229`) reads `redirect` from the return path that `keptReturnPath` already accepted. It then passes that value through `keptReturnPath` again, the same function the door uses for `callbackURL` (`:187-212`). That rule needs one leading `/`, and rejects `//`, a backslash, a control character, any of these behind up to three layers of percent-encoding, and a parser-resolved path that starts with `//`. A scheme such as `javascript:` fails the leading-`/` test.
- *Checked again before use.* The value is read with `URL.searchParams`, which decodes it once, and is checked by the rule again at that point. If `redirect` appears more than once, nothing is carried.
- *Encoded, never concatenated.* `signInPageUrl` (`:233-238`) builds the query with `URLSearchParams.set`. Both the vendor's `errorCallbackURL` (`:432`) and the door's own landing (`:412`) go through it. The base is `host.consolePageUrl('/login')`, so the origin is fixed by the server. better-auth adds its `error` with `appendQueryParams` (`oauth2/errors.mjs`, `api/routes/callback.mjs`, and the SSO plugin's OIDC callback), so an existing `?redirect=` keeps a correct `&` separator.
- *No new surface.* Anyone can already open `/login?redirect=<x>` directly. The server only carries a value its stricter rule accepts, and the Console still applies its own handling. A landing that carries `error` is a `hold`, so the page does not start again (`directSignIn.ts:79`). The retry drops only `error` and `error_description`.
- *Scratch probe (a copy of the two functions, not a repo test).* These were all dropped: `//evil.example/x`, `https://evil.example/`, `/%2F%2Fevil.example`, `/\evil.example`, `\\evil.example`, `/%5cevil`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `/%09/evil`, `/..//evil` and `/%252f%252fevil`. A redirect of `/apps/crm?view=all` came back as `redirect=%2Fapps%2Fcrm%3Fview%3Dall`.

**Item 1: the floor counts what the page draws.**
- `pageOffersLocalSignIn` (`sign-in-method-floor.ts:130`) is `features.localSignIn !== 'off'`. The page uses the same test (`LoginForm.tsx:349`). It hides email and password, phone with a password, and phone OTP under `off`, whether or not `directSignIn` is on. The floor reads the same served config (`auth-plugin.ts:2335`, `getPublicConfig()`), and `localSignIn` is served only while the direct sign-in setting is on. So "phone is excluded only under `off`" is exactly the page's rule. Under `hidden`, the page still offers both at `/login?local=1`.
- *Too strict?* No. The refusal fires only under `off`, with enterprise SSO on, on the last provider row, and with no social or OIDC provider and no host handoff. In that state, deleting the row leaves the page with nothing to draw. A refused delete locks nobody out, and every way to recover stays open.
- *Too loose?* No longer. Before this PR, `off` with phone on passed the delete and the boot report. That is fixed.
- `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` is a standard code (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts:97`; the ledger synonym is in `error-code-ledger.test.ts:313`). The PR does not add a new code.
- `enterpriseSsoLocalOff` is in all 11 locales (`:284`, `:304`, `:326`, `:352`, `:373`, `:394`, `:418`, `:444`, `:469`, `:494`, `:518`). It is a required field of `SignInFloorCopy`, so typecheck holds the set.

**must-fix M1: under `off` with email and password switched off, the new refusal and the new boot report give a remedy that does not work, and a pin locks it in.**
- The message is chosen by `config.emailPassword?.enabled !== false` (`sign-in-method-floor.ts:763`). The boot report is branched the same way (`:787`). Under `off` with email and password off, the delete gets `enterpriseSso`, whose first remedy is "First turn email and password sign-in back on". The boot report gets the original text, which says "no phone-number sign-in" and "Recover: set OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED=true and restart" (`:799-806`).
- Under `off`, neither remedy helps. Turning email and password on only moves the next attempt to the `enterpriseSsoLocalOff` refusal. With phone on, "no phone-number sign-in" is false. This PR newly refuses that state (phone on, email and password off, `off`) and newly reports it. The pin at `sign-in-method-floor.test.ts:811-815` asserts the `enterpriseSso` copy there.
- The PR body gives the reason for the new copy as "turn email and password sign-in back on does nothing there". The same reason applies to this case.
- `sso.mdx:722` ("Recover by setting `OS_AUTH_DIRECT_SIGN_IN_LOCAL_PATH=hidden`") is also not enough in this state.
- Fix:
  - Choose the copy and the report branch by `!pageOffersLocalSignIn(config)`.
  - Give the `off` texts a remedy that holds in both states. For example: set the local sign-in path back to `hidden`, and also turn email and password on if it is off. Or add a third variant.
  - Re-pin the phone-only-under-`off` case and add a boot case for `off` with email and password off.
  - Word the docs sentence to match.

### ② Semver level

- *`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right.* A delete that returned 200 now returns `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` under `off`. Two pins hold this, each with its CONTROL (`sign-in-method-floor.test.ts:660-685`). The title carries `!`.
- The changeset (`:13`) has a BREAKING paragraph that names who is affected (direct sign-in with the local path `off`) and the fix (`:17`). It has exactly one `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) ... -->` marker (`:11`). No stored key or metadata moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` are right.
- The redirect change only widens: a landing that was the bare page now carries a value the page already had. It is described in prose under "Also fixed" (`:19`).

### ③ Boundary flags

- The diff touches only plugin-auth sources, tests, one changeset and one docs page. It touches no `packages/spec`, protocol, generated file or release-owned page. `sso.mdx` is outside the claim's file surface, as declared.
- The dogfood battery is reported green at this head (467 files / 3950 passed). I did not run it.
- Still open on the card: items 2 and 5, and the settings save (`signInMethodFloorPredicate`, `sign-in-method-floor.ts:631`), which still counts email and password under `off`.

**Nits (none blocks).**
- N1. The changeset's "Widened" list (`:7`) does not name the new served copy `enterpriseSsoLocalOff` (11 locales) or the `asThePageOffers` option of `otherSignInMethods`. It also calls `pageOffersLocalSignIn`, `pageOffersEmailPassword` and `carriedRedirect` "public functions". They are module exports only: `src/index.ts:97` exports just two types from `direct-sign-in`, and nothing from `sign-in-method-floor`. Say "module exports", and add the copy key in prose.
- N2. The foreign-redirect pin (`direct-sign-in.test.ts:310`) loops over 3 spellings. Loop it over `FOREIGN_RETURN_PATHS` (`:56-80`) instead, so the backslash, `javascript:`, control-character and `/..//` spellings are pinned through `carriedRedirect` too. Today they hold only because `carriedRedirect` delegates to `keptReturnPath`.
- N3. `sso.mdx:717-718` says "the checks that keep a way to sign in do not count it under `off`". The settings save still counts it. Name the two checks this PR changes, and mention phone sign-in too.
- N4. The BREAKING paragraph (`:13`) does not name phone sign-in. A deployment under `off` with email and password off and phone on is also newly refused and newly reported. Also, the exits it lists under `off` (another provider row, a social or OIDC provider, a host handoff) have no pin under `off`. In the code, `asThePageOffers` gates only phone, so they hold today.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cc741c8ef32ceca989c36dbe42bbcad2c74fe798`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `.changeset/33358-local-sign-in-off-floor.md`, `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/direct-sign-in.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts`

This reviews the delta `2a03b651...cc741c8e` (one commit, `cc741c8e`, 5 files, +61/−38) against my FAIL at `2a03b651` (comment 6888499485). I read the diff and the code it relies on at the head: `resolveDirectSignIn` (`direct-sign-in.ts:141-162`), `keptReturnPath` and `carriedRedirect` (`:187-229`), `pageOffersLocalSignIn` and `pageOffersEmailPassword` (`sign-in-method-floor.ts:130-137`), and `otherSignInMethods` (`:228-238`). I ran no repo test or build. CI at this head was still running when I posted (25 passed, 11 in progress, 2 queued, none failed).

### ① Derived judgments

**M1: closed.**
- *Selection.* The delete copy is now `pageOffersLocalSignIn(config) ? enterpriseSso : enterpriseSsoLocalOff` (`sign-in-method-floor.ts:763`). The boot report branches on `!pageOffersLocalSignIn(config)` (`:787`). So under `off` the delete always gets `enterpriseSsoLocalOff`, and the boot report always gets the local-path text, whatever email and password says.
- *The `off` remedy is true.* `resolveDirectSignIn` reads `OS_AUTH_DIRECT_SIGN_IN_LOCAL_PATH` before `directSignIn.localSignIn` (`direct-sign-in.ts:147`), so `=hidden` replaces an `off` set in code. `getPublicConfig()` then serves `localSignIn: 'hidden'` (`auth-manager.ts:5928`), `pageOffersLocalSignIn` is true, and with email and password on, `pageOffersEmailPassword` is true. The page offers it at `/login?local=1`, and both checks stop firing. When email and password is off, the report adds `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED=true` (`:796-798`). That is the settings environment override, which wins over the stored value (`:71-73`), the same remedy the email-off branch already gave. The copy now says "set the local sign-in path back to hidden with email and password sign-in on", which holds in both states.
- *The other branch is now true too.* It is reached only when the page offers local sign-in and email and password is off. There, `asThePageOffers` counts phone (`:238`), so "no phone-number sign-in" is true whenever this text is printed.
- *Locales.* `enterpriseSsoLocalOff` changed in all 11 locales (en, zh-Hans, ja, es, zh-Hant, ar, fr, pt, ru, de, ko). I checked zh-Hans ("改回 hidden 并开启邮箱/密码登录"), zh-Hant, ja ("hidden に戻してメール/パスワードログインをオンにして"), es, fr and de. Each one adds "with email and password sign-in on" to the hidden remedy, as the English does, and no other sentence changed.
- *Pins.* The phone-only-under-`off` pin now expects `enterpriseSsoLocalOff`. It also expects the report to name both settings and not to say "no phone-number sign-in" (`sign-in-method-floor.test.ts:818-827`). A CONTROL with email and password off under `hidden` keeps `enterpriseSso` and the `OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED=true and restart` report (`:828-833`). A real-composition boot under `off` with email and password off expects one report that names both settings (`:694-699`). Each assertion matches the strings the code builds.
- *Docs.* `sso.mdx:717-726` now gives the same two-part remedy.

**No refuse/allow decision changed.** In both `ssoProviderDeleteRefusal` and `resolveNoSignInMethodReport`, every line that returns `undefined` or `null` is unchanged. The delta changes only which message a refusal or report carries. The decisions the earlier dogfood run covered are the same, so no new dogfood run is owed.

**Redirect: still safe.** `direct-sign-in.ts` is not in the delta. `carriedRedirect` still runs the value through `keptReturnPath` again, and `signInPageUrl` still builds the query with `URLSearchParams`. My earlier reasoning still holds.

**N1–N4: addressed.**
- N1. The changeset now says "module exports (not on the package entry)". `src/index.ts:97` still exports only the two `direct-sign-in` types. It also names `asThePageOffers` and the copy key `enterpriseSsoLocalOff` in 11 locales.
- N2. The pin is now `it.each(FOREIGN_RETURN_PATHS)`, over all 24 spellings (`direct-sign-in.test.ts:309`).
- N3. `sso.mdx` now names the two checks, includes phone sign-in, and says the settings save still counts email and password under `off`.
- N4. The BREAKING paragraph now says "and even with phone sign-in switched on".

**Nits (none blocks).**
- N5. One of the 24 spellings, `/${'a'.repeat(2048)}`, makes the whole `callbackURL` longer than `RETURN_PATH_MAX` (2048). `keptReturnPath` then drops the whole page path, so this case never reaches `carriedRedirect`. The assertion still holds, and the other 23 spellings do go through `carriedRedirect`.
- N6, carried over from the second half of N4. The exits under `off` (another provider row, a social or OIDC provider, a host handoff) still have no pin under `localSignIn: 'off'`. The `passes the delete with $name` table uses `OFF` (email and password off, no `localSignIn`). In the code, `asThePageOffers` gates only phone, so they hold today.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from my earlier record. `patch` with `fix(auth)!` and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right. The delta changes only refusal and report text, docs and pins. The new copy key existed before the delta, and only its text changed. The BREAKING paragraph and the "What to do" line now give the two-part remedy. There is still exactly one `adr-0087: not-required` marker. `Metadata-protocol: none` still holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The delta touches only plugin-auth source and tests, the changeset and `sso.mdx`. It does not touch `packages/spec`, any protocol or generated file, or any release-owned page.
- Still open on the card and outside this PR: items 2 and 5, and the settings save (`signInMethodFloorPredicate`, `sign-in-method-floor.ts:631`), which still counts email and password under `off`. `sso.mdx` now says so.

### ④ Design judgment

The delta makes the requested fix with the predicate the floor already uses, so the remedy is chosen by the rule the page uses to draw local sign-in. One copy key with a two-part remedy is enough. A third variant would add a locale set without telling the reader anything more. The boot report names the second setting only when it is needed, which keeps the common case short. The CONTROL under `hidden` makes sure the email-off copy cannot drift into the `off` text.
